prompts.1:
Art for a 2D top-down fantasy role-playing game. Bright, colorful medieval fantasy in clear daylight. Realistic proportions, nothing cartoonish, nothing grim. No text, no borders, no watermarks, no drop shadows.
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a reusable MODULAR ARCHITECTURE sprite sheet for Brasswake, region Tallyport.
REFERENCE ROLE: supplied image is the approved craftsmanship/style target ONLY. Do not copy a whole house, do not include its awning. Create individual fitted construction parts.
REGIONAL BUILDING MATERIALS: cream plaster between warm oak posts, rough stone footing, mottled orange terracotta tiles, carved oak frames and iron pegs.
REGIONAL DUNGEON MATERIALS: damp warm grey harbour ashlar, salt wear, restrained moss, oak supports.
Hand-painted fine pixel-art craftsmanship, crisp fine details, varied weathering, bevels, chips, mortar, material grain and small fasteners, coherent soft daylight upper left. NO flat generic filler strips.
Layout: exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 isolated objects evenly spaced in equal cells, no touching. Each piece centered in its cell with ample transparent clearance. No full buildings. All front panels flat front-facing and rectangular, camera above and slightly in front about 35 degrees. Not diagonal isometric; horizontal frontage and screen-vertical side rims.
TRUE transparent background. No ground, no shadow, no grass, nothing behind the character or object. No glow, haze or backdrop. No checkerboard image.

Exact row-major parts:
ROW1: (1) A rectangular plain ground-storey wall bay, regional wall material with structural vertical members at edges, narrow top rail/cornice and stone plinth at bottom. (2) Matching rectangular ground-storey window bay with one slim inset casement, rich frame and sill, matching plinth. (3) An elegant region-appropriate door surround, TWO narrow detailed jambs and one carved horizontal lintel, rectangular TRANSPARENT OPENING all the way through to bottom. No door leaf, no awning, canopy, hood, porch roof, foliage or projecting beams. Keep opening generous for an adult, frame only. (4) A tall narrow front-facing structural corner post/pilaster matching regional materials, detailed surface and slim stone foot; flat vertical strip, NOT a freestanding box.
ROW2: (1) An opaque square seamless repeat swatch of the regional ROOF material viewed overhead, four columns/four courses or panels, no frame; no perspective taper. (2) Long horizontal narrow ridge cap run made from the regional roof material with overlapping joints, fitted collars/bindings and weathered relief, isolated with no underlying roof. (3) A long horizontal front eave: one thin roof lip over a richly detailed fascia/cornice, small structural ends, no full roof or wall. (4) A long NARROW VERTICAL side-eave strip, roof edge on right half and detailed fascia rim on left half; runs vertically on screen, no diagonal wedge and no full roof.
ROW3: (1) Rectangular matching upper-storey plain wall bay with detailed top/bottom structural rails, NO stone footing. (2) Matching upper-storey window bay with two slim inset windows and detailed frame and rails, NO footing. (3) A small regional masonry chimney with narrow fitted textured metal apron at base and tiny side returns; chimney emerges through roof, no roof slab behind it. Rich worn masonry, shaped flashing with folds and subtle highlights, NO flat gray rectangle. (4) A tall rectangular region-appropriate wooden/metal door leaf with detailed boards/panels, iron/bronze hinges, handle and edge thickness; no surrounding frame.
ROW4: (1) An opaque rectangular reusable DUNGEON WALL FACE module in dungeon materials, carefully laid varied ashlar courses, subtle weathering and mortar. Front-facing modular masonry, no floor or scenery, edges flush and repeatable. (2) Long horizontal narrow DUNGEON COPING module matching that wall, dressed stone top with bevels, carved band where appropriate, thickness, varied worn edges, no wall below. (3) A complete broad ascending STAIR PASSAGE module in dungeon materials: region-appropriate framed arch/lintel and jambs, a wide walkable ground-level landing at its front, steps rising AWAY into a recessed passage, a tiny hint of light at top. Adult-sized aperture. No staircase sticking out of a flat house. Transparent outside the passage; inside the opening is actual dark recess, no background outside it. (4) A separate descending STAIR OPENING module in dungeon materials: broad low stone curb on three sides around a dark open mouth, visible treads receding DOWN away from viewer, a clear generous front landing edge. No tall doorway. Transparent outside actual stones/opening. It must work both on a dungeon floor and as an outdoor cellar entrance, with no surrounding ground.

Every minor fitting must have the same rich painted finish as the reference. Keep silhouettes clean, geometry coherent, stone courses and rails consistent. No labels, numbers, interface or decorative scenery. No awnings or canopies anywhere.
